label: Atlantium Sand-boxer
note: Issue #42: the one speeder Skrugs sells. Read by src/systems/vehicles/hover_model.gd (how it moves) and speeder_node.gd (how it looks, its hull and guns). It rides `hover_height` above whatever is under it (sand, floors, ramp tops) and turns ballistic when the ground drops away faster than it can follow (`launch_gap` in one frame): off the end of a ramp or over a dune crest. There is no jump button; low gravity makes it a light, floaty sled. No fall or crash damage: only gunfire hurts it. Issue #43: look.scene is the Hyper3D speeder (assets/vehicles/speeder.glb); the primitive sled is the fallback. label is its make and model from the name generator. Issue #82: the Atlantium Sand-boxer replaces the Curlew (assets/vehicles/sandboxer*.glb, one Hyper3D model in four paint jobs from content/look/vehicle_models.json). look.paints names them; SpeederNode takes one by name (empty = look.scene). Skrugs's speeders go round `sold_paints`; the Remnant's black and red one is parked outside the front gate (the 'remnant_speeder' marker in port_town.json). Issue #627: `look.stand_in` is the primitive sled built when there is no model (its pieces: box or cyl, size, at, rot in degrees, which look colour, `mirror` for both sides; `fan` is the spinning rear fan), and `sleep_distance` is how far every player must be before a parked one stops stepping its hover. racer.json and hauler.json are the other models Skrugs sells. Issue #609: `seats` are where NPC riders sit, in the speeder's own frame (x right, y up, z back; their feet, sunk into the tub): the driver, and a second rider behind (content/core/vehicles/speeder_drivers.json drives it). Issue #618: drafting: inside another speeder's tow (within tow_m behind it, within tow_cone_deg of its tail) the draft builds over tow_build_s and lifts top speed by tow_speed and acceleration by tow_accel (shares). fov is the chase camera's, widened by up to fov_kick degrees while boosting.
